summary_text: We looked at 112 skills in this repo (all local; SSS manages none yet). This run was on a pull-request branch under review in which two skills changed: fleet-upgrade-verification, whose readiness check grew a registry of per-entry rules from the upgrade-failure catalogue with an audit-log reader and a first rule (a zonal control plane, reported as a risk that never blocks), and the shipped copy of gke-upgrades, whose appended section now points at that registry. We wrote new coverage summaries for those two and scored their 221 pairs; the other 5,995 pair scores came from the cache. The rescoring moved nothing: the two skills remain 3 stars apart (declared counterparts, one executes and one advises), the shipped and upstream gke-upgrades copies remain 1 star apart, and no new pair fell to 2 stars or lower, so the changed skills add no new overlap with the rest of the set. Across all 6,216 pairs, 29 score 2 stars or lower, 16 of them byte-identical upstream-and-shipped copies of a gke-* skill. What the changed skills add: an agent can now ask one script for drain-blocking PDBs, maintenance exclusions and windows, node-pool skew and the catalogue rules in one pass, per member, with per-kind read errors so a cut pod list costs only the rules that need pods, and gke-upgrades tells its reader to carry those rows into the plan rather than check them by hand. What they break or risk: the new fleet-upgrade-verification text contradicts its own scripts once (it says three reads are skipped after a failed PDB read where the code and its own list say four) and one new sentence about a rule's own reads is easy to misread, both in lines this pull request added; with --readiness, exit 0 no longer means every read succeeded, which fleet-upgrade-verification states but gke-upgrades does not; the SKILL.md spends a paragraph on the audit-log read and the "other blockers" column although the only registered rule reads the cluster record alone and can never block; and the appended section's older claim that the script reads with gcloud container only and writes one file still disagrees with the script, which this change did not touch. Everything else in this report is unchanged from the run at the merge base: the gke-* skills are generated from third_party/google-skills/ plus overlay patches and SSS does not yet know that tree is a source, so the duplicates and most conflicts are that pipeline seen from outside, and the five hand-maintained copies under agents/cluster/skills/ still drift from the shipped copies. A second, sceptical pass re-read every finding against its quoted evidence: of 65 findings it kept 65, changed 5 (it dropped the unfinished-sentence claim from the new fleet-upgrade-verification finding, downgraded the new gke-upgrades finding to likely and the drift-detection finding to unsure, and replaced two non-verbatim quotes), and deleted none. Nothing was changed in the repo: this run was report-only by request.
